reading: 22.27 of 26 configurations produce byte-distinct streams on average, a collision rate of 0.143 against the javac failure's 1.0. The channel is real. Note the structure: base64 and binary content collapse to roughly 14 distinct streams because when there is nothing to match, encoders converge on stored or near-minimal blocks - mechanistically expected, and it caps what is achievable on incompressible content.
what: A1 channel-capacity check for the carved-DEFLATE thesis, run BEFORE building any corpus. The cheapest possible falsification: if the 26 configurations produce identical streams, the label is not a function of the input and no volume of data can help.
why_it_matters: The archived trial killed a candidate on exactly this failure - javac 17.0.8 and 17.0.13 at --release 8 produced 345 of 345 BYTE-IDENTICAL class files, a channel of zero capacity. This is that same test, run first rather than last.
